steps.label: Width = number of qubits (wires) a circuit uses
steps.sub: A strict admission requirement — a 50-qubit circuit can't run on a 20-qubit device

steps.label: Depth = the longest chain of sequentially-dependent gates
steps.sub: Not the total gate count — the number of required time-layers

steps.label: Gates on disjoint qubits can share a layer
steps.sub: No shared control, no shared target — they run in parallel

steps.label: Gates sharing a qubit cannot share a layer
steps.sub: A qubit passes through only one gate at a time

code:
q1: --H--*--
q2: --H--X--
q3: ---------

width = 3   (three wires, q3 has no gates)
depth = 2   (both H's share layer 1; CNOT needs layer 2)
caption: Depth tracks dependency chains, not raw gate count.

steps.label: Qubits slowly lose information to their environment
steps.sub: Decoherence, plus small errors accumulating with every gate

steps.label: Each sequential layer is real execution time
steps.sub: More layers means more time for noise and error to corrupt the state

steps.label: Compilers and transpilers work hard to reduce depth
steps.sub: Sometimes even using MORE gates, if more of them run in parallel

steps.label: Chapter 6 revisits this exact tension
steps.sub: An idealized simulator has no depth-driven error cost; real hardware does

subtitle: Why a small, fixed set of native gates is enough to build anything.
